title: Production Incident: Cascading Lock Pileup Caused by Missing Foreign Key Index
realWorldScenario: During a customer account deletion workflow, a batch script deletes 1,000 inactive accounts from `customers`. Within 10 seconds, the entire payment API freezes. Investigation shows that deleting a row from `customers` triggers a table-wide `ShareLock` or sequential scan on `orders`.
questionStatement: Explain how PostgreSQL enforces foreign key constraints during DELETE/UPDATE of parent rows. Why does a foreign key column without an index on the child table cause table-level lock contention and cascading API outages? Write the query to detect all unindexed foreign keys across the database.

symptoms: API freeze during customer account deletions
Hundreds of INSERT/UPDATE transactions queued on orders table
pg_stat_activity shows DELETE FROM customers waiting on locks
High disk I/O on orders heap table
candidateTasks: Explain why PostgreSQL must scan child table on parent DELETE
Demonstrate that PostgreSQL does NOT automatically index foreign keys
Provide the system catalog query to identify all unindexed foreign keys
Generate DDL to create missing indexes CONCURRENTLY

expectedConcepts: Child table scan on parent row deletion
PostgreSQL does NOT automatically index foreign keys
Full sequential scan of child table under lock for every deleted parent row
System catalog query comparing pg_constraint with pg_index
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY on foreign key column
hints: Does PostgreSQL create an index on child table foreign key columns automatically?
What must the database do when you delete a customer with 10 million orders in the database?
